newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget issues remain unresolved.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget issues remain unresolved.

text.p: White House and Republican leaders have yet to resolve final details on the budget agreement, but expect the remaining issues will be settled by the end of Wednesday, Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle and White House congressional liason John Hilley said.

Speaking with reporters, Hilley said the $135 billion gross tax cut would be primarily used for a child tax credit and $35 billion worth of education credits. Republicans have said the tax legislation to be worked out later in the year will include a capital gains tax rate cut and some form of a reduction in inheritance taxes.

"I think you'll see some written commitments here in the next day or two about the overall parameters of the approaches to the tax bill," Hilley told reporters. He spoke at Daschle's regular news conference.
"We feel confident that this will be a good tax bill. The vast part of the tax bill will be going toward education and the child credit," he added.
Issues remaining unresolved include policy changes in the Medicare program and questions on approprations levels.
Daschle predicted the final plan will win overwhelming support of Senate Democrats. "By and large, well over three-fourths of our caucus will support this budget agreement."

Negotiations are also continuing on Republican efforts to pass an automatic spending bill, which would keep the government funded at 98 percent of this year's level for fiscal 1998 (beginning October 1, 1997) if regular spending bills have not been approved.

The dispute has held up passage of emergency disaster relief for 23 states, including the flooded areas in the upper Midwest. President Clinton has threatened to veto the bill if this automatic spending provision and other controversial amendments dealing with the environment and the census are not removed.
If the automatic spending bill is passed in some form, Democrats would like to see funding assured at the levels set in the budget agreement reached last Friday.
"We have bargained in good faith to reach this, and now anything that's done automatically must be consistent with that," he said.
